geographyNote: City of Victoria, British Columbia (census subdivision)

facts.text: In 2023, total revenues in Greater Victoria's tech industry were estimated at $5.9 billion, and the sector employed more than 20,000 people, about 2,000 of them self-employed.
Victoria is home to upwards of 500 active tech companies, about 15 per cent of the BC sector, and VIATEC has set a goal of reaching $10 billion in annual revenue by 2030.
Visitors spent over $1.9 billion in the Victoria region, and the Victoria Conference Centre recorded just over 94,000 delegate days in 2024, a 12% increase from 84,000 in 2023.
The BC Public Service, headquartered in Victoria, is the largest single employer in the province with over 35,000 regular and auxiliary employees.
The Downtown Victoria Business Association is a Business Improvement Area established by municipal bylaw in 2005; every business within its boundaries is automatically a member.

overview: The City of Victoria had 91,867 residents in the 2021 Census, up 7.1 percent from 85,792 in 2016, on only 19.45 square kilometres at the tip of Vancouver Island. It is a city of small households: 49,222 occupied dwellings for that population means many people live alone, the median age is 42.8, and the median household income was $67,500 in 2020.

The provincial government, a fast-growing technology sector and year-round tourism supply the customers. Because the city proper is only the urban core of a larger region, a local business serves downtown workers, visitors and condo dwellers while competing with suburban rivals in Saanich and Langford.
